hints.title: Window Between Requests
hints.text: A user actively requests messages if two distinct requests occur within 24 hours (86,400 seconds) of one another.

hints.title: Pairing Consecutive Requests
hints.text: Self-join confirmations on user_id where the second timestamp is strictly greater than the first timestamp.

hints.title: Elapsed Time Condition
hints.text: Check timestamp difference between the two events to ensure it is at most 24 hours.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT DISTINCT
    c1.user_id
FROM Confirmations c1
JOIN Confirmations c2
    ON c1.user_id = c2.user_id
    AND c1.time_stamp < c2.time_stamp
    AND TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, c1.time_stamp, c2.time_stamp) <= 86400;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) if utilizing an index on (user_id, time_stamp)
complexity.space: O(U) space for distinct qualifying user IDs
complexity.notes: Self-join on timestamp difference within 86400 seconds.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing timestamps with identical equality can produce false zero-second intervals.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Inequality join with TIMESTAMPDIFF handles boundaries cleanly.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should account for exact 24-hour limits and distinct user outputs.

solutions.code:
SELECT DISTINCT
    c1.user_id
FROM Confirmations c1
JOIN Confirmations c2
    ON c1.user_id = c2.user_id
    AND c1.time_stamp < c2.time_stamp
    AND TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, c1.time_stamp, c2.time_stamp) <= 86400;

SELECT DISTINCT
    c1.user_id
FROM Confirmations c1
JOIN Confirmations c2
    ON c1.user_id = c2.user_id
    AND c1.time_stamp < c2.time_stamp
    AND EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (c2.time_stamp - c1.time_stamp)) <= 86400;
